role: wave 2, domain 8 (dense / sparse CC bombers, early INT86 heavy bombs), R1-verify
base: rev0 = V6nohunt (A 194 B sha 6861894f, B 202 B sha 8579e2c2)

mechanism.anchor_bytes: Each generation's anchor is the 2-byte far call FF 1F (call far [bx]) written by stosw (AX=1FFFh) at arena P with P mod 100h = 52h for A and B (and captured zombies). A dwells ~256 calls per generation (400h trail / 4), B ~512 (800h trail). A CC on P (FF -> CC = INT3) kills the process; a CC on P+1 only gives FF CC = dec sp, so P itself is the critical byte.
mechanism.why_52h_is_pinned: The rebuild trigger is the low byte of the pushed return IP: it must be A4h (MOVSB), so the anchor IP must be ..A2h; arena offset = IP + 16*FAR_SEG - 10000h, FAR_SEG 0FFBh -> in-page 52h. The in-page offset can only change in 10h steps via FAR_SEG (0FF6h..1000h usable, B055), so every V6-style anchor sits on an address = 2 (mod 10h).
mechanism.IND_BRA: official-2025/survivors-online/IND_BRA1/2 (25 B, identical): mov byte [si],CCh; add si,23h; cmp si,0FF00h; jb; restart at 0400h. Both warriors bomb the same lattice {400h+23h*k} in lockstep (copies add nothing), one byte per 3 rounds, full pass ~5500 rounds. Its own 25-byte body usually contains a lattice point, so it tends to bomb itself.

threatFindings.threat: IND_BRA (step-23h single-byte CC sweep) takes points from rev0 by hitting the anchor
threatFindings.evidence: foy12 (8 cohorts x 20 battles, IND_BRA + 2 random 2025 teams): IND_BRA team score 0.000 in every cohort; base team 0.806 (A 0.394, B 0.413); the losses come from the other opponents (e.g. cohort #5 Baltika9 10 + Grindo 3 -> base 0.35). Screen field S cohort sthreat-bomb_IND_BRA: base 0.967. Static: lockstep copies bomb one fixed lattice; per A generation the anchor is on that lattice with p ~1/35 and the sweep passes during the dwell with p ~0.05.
threatFindings.impact: none measurable; not worth any defense bytes

threatFindings.threat: Early INT86 heavy bombs hit our load image before we leave it (startup deaths)
threatFindings.evidence: Base trace nightTR-6861894f3c-8579e2c221 (job 20261003182659506-B051-trace-pkj3o, re-read with scratch/B058/early.mjs): A_HRZ_Underflow1 INT86 CCCC block at round 7 kills CAND1 at round 8 (cs 1000h, ip-load 14h, 8 x CC, cohort sthreat-movsw_cgx123123); A_GSA_GhostBytes_0x1 INT86 zero block at round 7 corrupts A's image -> death round 68 at ip-load 8Bh (s2025-3); A_RZL_YANDE2 INT86 pattern CC E2 2A CC at round 34 -> CAND1 dies round 34 at ip-load 39h (s2025-1). Also zom20b/c/d writes hit B's image at rounds 19-51 (4 startup deaths of CAND2 at ip-load 8Fh-B4h). Field scan: 37 warriors in the 2025 field carry CD 86; early users (INT86 in the first 20h bytes) include KosherCode, Ctrl_Alt_Elite, Underflow, stack_attack2, K0F1M, TOM_AND_JERRY, YANDE, GoonSquad, Code_Jokers4Life.
threatFindings.impact: 3 of 161 base deaths (~2%) from opponent INT86 bombs in startup, plus ~4 from zombie writes. Placement is random, so the only lever is time spent in the load image (A001 already showed faster startup is mixed: +0.017 on 2025, -0.025 on strong). No fix proposed.

threatFindings.threat: A page-lattice CC bomber tuned to the fixed anchor in-page offset 52h wipes out rev0
threatFindings.evidence: foy12: B058_pg52 (42 B per warrior) -> base team 0.025 (8 cohorts; 6 of 8 exactly 0) vs 0.8625 for the identical bomber at in-page 12h (control). Causal check ktxof: moving the anchor to in-page 22h (FAR_SEG 0FF8h) gives +0.677 vs pg52 and -0.819 vs pg22, so the hole moves exactly with the anchor byte. Critical byte: FF at arena P (P mod 100h = 52h) written by stosw AX=1FFFh in phoenix_init and in the worker (stosw; dec di; call far [bx]).
threatFindings.impact: Catastrophic if any opponent ever targets in-page 52h; also hits every V6-family warrior (V6, V4, V6Guard), which share 52h. No 2025 field warrior does this, so the field effect today is zero.

threatFindings.threat: Choosing another FAR_SEG (or randomizing it) closes the bomber hole
threatFindings.evidence: 7v9o9: B058_pgall16 (35 B) bombs every address = 2 mod 10h, i.e. every position a V6-style anchor can take: base team 0.519 (A 0.346, B 0.173) vs ~0.86 with the control, even though the bomber itself scores only 0.05. ktxof shows a fixed shift only moves the hole; B055 oauc2 shows the shift itself costs ALL -0.0105.
threatFindings.impact: The weakness is architectural (a 1-byte-critical anchor dwelling 256/512 rounds at a fixed address); B, with the longer 800h dwell, is hit twice as often as A. A real defense would need a different trigger design or shorter dwell (shorter dwell already rejected by A004).

recommendation: No promote-candidate from B058. IND_BRA is not a threat to rev0 (not-reproduced). Early INT86 startup kills are real but small (~2% of deaths) and placement-random; no cheap fix. Main result: a verified architectural hole. A 35-42 byte CC bomber on the anchor lattice (2 mod 10h, or exactly 52h) cuts rev0 from ~0.86 to 0.52 (generic) or 0.03 (tuned). Nothing in the 2025 field does this, so today's ranking is unchanged, but keep scratch/B058/pg52 and pgall16 as robustness probes for any future base (they also hit V6/V4/V6Guard). Do not spend jobs on FAR_SEG shifts or randomization as a fix.
